name: dashboard-grid
import: import { DashboardGrid, DashboardCatalog, type DashboardItem } from '@absoluteui/components/dashboard-grid';
purpose: Enhances a host whose children carry data-aui-item="<id>" into a responsive column grid (a labelled region). Items are placed with CSS grid placement written through the CSSOM. In edit mode each item gets a move handle button (pointer drag, or press it and use the arrow keys; Shift+arrows resize) and a pointer-only corner resize grip; other items are pushed down and float up (vertical compaction); locked items never move. Layouts are stored per breakpoint (default lg 1024 px / 12 columns, md 640 px / 6, sm 0 / 1), derived for narrower breakpoints when not saved, serializable through `layouts` and aui-layout-change, and undoable (moves and resizes). The DOM is reordered to the visual reading order after every change, keeping focus. The same subpath exports DashboardCatalog (an add-widget list of templates, by click, Enter, Space, or drag onto the grid) and the pure layout functions (collides, clampItem, sortLayout, compactLayout, resolveLayout, findFreeSpot, adaptLayout).
whenToUse: User-arrangeable dashboards of widgets (KPI cards, charts, tables) whose layout is saved per user.
Fixed, responsive dashboard layouts defined in column/row units that must adapt to narrower screens.
Letting users add widgets from a catalog of templates (DashboardCatalog).
whenNotToUse: Simple responsive page layout without user rearrangement: use CSS grid or the Layout component.
Reordering a single vertical list: use Sortable List.
Free-form canvases with pixel positioning, overlapping items, or rotation.
responsive: A ResizeObserver on the host picks the breakpoint with the largest minWidth not above the host content width (default lg 1024 px / 12 columns, md 640 px / 6, sm 0 / 1). A breakpoint without a stored layout derives one from the widest: positions and widths scale proportionally and a single column stacks items in reading order. Changing breakpoint cancels a grab and emits aui-breakpoint-change. Row height (default 80 px) and gap (default 16 px) are fixed CSS px values. Handles and grips are touch-target-min squares.
rtl: Columns run from the inline start. With direction 'rtl', ArrowLeft/ArrowRight moves are mirrored and pointer coordinates are measured from the right edge; the resize grip is mirrored (nesw-resize cursor). Shift+ArrowRight widens and Shift+ArrowLeft narrows an item in both directions.
theme: Handles use color-surface, color-border-strong and radius-sm; a grabbed handle (aria-pressed=true) uses color-selected with color-selected-text and a border, not color alone. The drop placeholder is color-selected with a dashed color-focus-ring border. The dragged item gets shadow-lg. Forced-colors mode uses Canvas/Highlight for the placeholder and grabbed handle and CanvasText for the grip. Item transitions are removed under reduced motion and data-aui-animation='none'.
security: Positions are written with style.setProperty (grid-column, grid-row, translate, custom properties), never style attributes or HTML; CSP-safe. Labels and announcements use textContent/attributes only. Items, layouts, and breakpoints are validated (DASHBOARD_GRID_OPTIONS) before use, so saved layouts from storage can be passed back safely; malformed input throws instead of rendering. Catalog template labels and descriptions render as text.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry. The grid reports layouts (aui-layout-change detail.layouts, or the layouts getter); the application stores them. Item content is owned by the page or framework and never moved into or out of the host except for DOM reordering within the host.

budgets.budget: < 40 ms in headless Chromium (e2e performance test)

budgets.metric: One keyboard move step with 50 items
budgets.budget: < 16 ms in headless Chromium (e2e performance test)

performance.testedScale: 50 items for the performance budgets; 3 to 4 items in the behavior unit tests.

limitations: Vertical compaction: an item cannot rest below empty space, and a full-width item cannot pass a half-width neighbor (it floats back); use compaction 'none' for free placement.
Collisions push items down only, never sideways.
Undo and redo cover geometry (moves, resizes, setLayout); they do not add back removed items or remove added ones.
In edit mode Ctrl/Cmd+Z, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z, and Ctrl/Cmd+Y are handled on the whole host, including text fields inside widgets.
Pointer grabs and drops are not announced; keyboard grabs, moves, resizes, drops, and cancels are (assertive).
The resize grip is pointer-only (aria-hidden); keyboard users resize with Shift+arrow keys on the move handle.
No auto-scroll while dragging near the viewport edge.
The breakpoint at create time uses host.clientWidth; a host that is not laid out yet starts at the narrowest breakpoint until the ResizeObserver reports its width.
update() with items, layouts, or breakpoints replaces all stored layouts.
Manual screen-reader verification (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) is pending.
unsupported: Overlapping items, pixel positioning, or nesting grids inside items as linked layouts.
HTML5 drag and drop (the catalog uses pointer events; files cannot be dropped).
antiPatterns: Setting reorderDom: false without another way to keep focus order equal to visual order (WCAG 1.3.2, 2.4.3).
Re-passing a new items array on every render in a framework: update({ items }) replaces the stored layouts; keep items stable or feed back detail.layouts.
Relying on drag alone: the move handle's keyboard path must stay available.

adapters.angular: @absoluteui/angular/dashboard-grid: hand-written AuiDashboardGrid directive ([auiDashboardGrid], enhances the host in place; outputs auiLayoutChange, auiBreakpointChange) and AuiDashboardCatalog directive ([auiDashboardCatalog], input grid).
adapters.react: @absoluteui/react/dashboard-grid: hand-written AuiDashboardGrid (renders a <div>; props = DashboardGridOptions + children with data-aui-item + onLayoutChange/onBreakpointChange; ref receives the DashboardGrid). Catalog: @absoluteui/react/dashboard-catalog AuiDashboardCatalog (grid, label, templates, create, onCatalogAdd).
adapters.vue: @absoluteui/vue/dashboard-grid: AuiDashboardGrid (default slot; emits layoutChange, breakpointChange; template ref exposes controller). Catalog: @absoluteui/vue/dashboard-catalog AuiDashboardCatalog (emits catalogAdd with the DOM event).
